title: Microsoft Purview DLP: file creation and modification date conditions for SharePoint and OneDrive
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, DLP conditions, permissions and licensing are supported, and the documentation gaps were independently checked. Minor corrections should restore the administrative-scope heading in the path and identify the quarantine example as preview.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview DLP for SharePoint and OneDrive gains file creation and modification date predicates that can target new, recently edited or older content.
claims.quote: These conditions allow admins to configure policies based on when the files were created or last modified, enabling policies that target newly created documents, recently edited files, or older content that may require stricter governance.

claims.claim: A DLP rule can combine content conditions with date conditions.
claims.quote: Conditions can be grouped and joined by boolean operators (AND, OR, NOT) so that you define a rule by stating what should be included and then defining exclusions in a different group joined to the first by a NOT.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; summary; What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet document creation or modification date conditions on either the UI or automation surface of SharePoint and OneDrive auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling creation modification date conditions SharePoint OneDrive New-AutoSensitivityLabelRule AdvancedRule. Read apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, New-AutoSensitivityLabelRule and Set-AutoSensitivityLabelRule syntax; no date predicate or configuring syntax.

claims.claim: The auto-labeling article lists Document created by as the one extra SharePoint and OneDrive advanced-rule condition.
claims.quote: If your location is SharePoint sites or OneDrive accounts and you selected Advanced rules, there is one other condition that you can select: ... Document created by

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A rule restricted to modification dates on or after a cut-off excludes files with modification dates before that cut-off.
claims.quote: Document modification date is on or after ... Conditions are where you define what you want the rule to look for and the context in which those items are being used.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn does not describe whether background updates count toward the modification date used by this condition.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP modification date background; Purview DLP creation modification date conditions licensing meter price background updates relative dates. Read dlp-policy-reference date passages and search results; no background-update semantics for this predicate.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes policy date predicates rather than a new identity or sharing mechanism.
claims.quote: With these new date-based predicates, Purview DLP delivers stronger lifecycle-aware protection, improved policy accuracy, and greater flexibility in securing data across SPOD.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Matching conditions cause a rule's configured actions to be taken, including access restrictions.
claims.quote: it's a match and the rest of the actions in the policy should be taken on it. ... Supported actions: SharePoint ... Restrict access or encrypt the content in Microsoft 365 locations ... Block everyone

claims.claim: Quarantine is an example of a configured DLP action for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: The features described in this article are in preview. This article walks you through the prerequisites and configuration for using the DLP file quarantine action for SharePoint and OneDrive locations.
claims.fix: Replace 'such as restricting access or quarantine' with 'such as restricting access' to avoid presenting the separately licensed preview quarantine action as an unqualified example.
